studies.title: Inputs present and readable
studies.question: Will any of the rest of this run at all?
studies.attack: You are reporting numbers from files nobody can find.
studies.note: Writes no result. It is the precondition for everything else.

studies.title: Outcome distribution and the error brackets
studies.question: How is life expectancy distributed, and where does the model's error sit against that spread?
studies.attack: An R-squared of 0.67 on a variable with a narrow range is not an achievement.

studies.title: Census of every multi-statistic field
studies.question: Across every field described by more than one summary statistic, which description takes the attribution?
studies.attack: You found one striking pair and wrote a paper about it.

studies.title: Learner and hyperparameter table
studies.question: What exactly was fitted, with which settings, against which alternatives?
studies.attack: You do not say what model this is or why it was chosen.

studies.title: The two night-cooling constructions are not the same column
studies.question: Are the two night-cooling variables a duplicate under two names?
studies.attack: Your two night-cooling variables are the same thing and you have counted it twice.

studies.title: Frozen panels: what the model actually saw
studies.question: Which columns are in the model, and can the exact modelling table be exported so an outside analyst starts where we did?
studies.attack: Nobody can reproduce this because nobody knows which columns survived your filters.
studies.note: Also the guard against the mistake of starting from the master CSV and skipping the gate, which inflates the score.

studies.title: The formaldehyde pair before any model is fitted
studies.question: What is true about the pair from the data alone, with no model in the way?
studies.attack: Everything you say about that pair is a property of your model, not of the air.

studies.title: The located crossings, west and east
studies.question: Do the turning points land in the same place in the arid half of the country and the humid half?
studies.attack: Your thresholds are an average over two different climates and mean nothing in either.

studies.title: Does the duration advantage follow atmospheric lifetime?
studies.question: Is the advantage of a duration metric concentrated in the short-lived species, as atmospheric chemistry predicts?
studies.attack: You split twenty species at two days, which you chose, and got one-sided p = 0.006. Choose three days and tell me again.
studies.note: Sweeps the cutoff, gives a cutoff-free rank test with a permutation p, perturbs every lifetime value by an order of magnitude, and jackknifes over species.

studies.title: Where the admission rules were placed
studies.question: Does the admitted set, and the survival of the central comparison, depend on where the coverage gate and the correlation cut were put?
studies.attack: Ninety-five per cent coverage and a cut at 0.98 are arbitrary and were chosen after you saw the result.

studies.title: Five reference models
studies.question: What does a mean, a linear model, a single tree, a random forest and the production model each score?
studies.attack: You have not shown that any of this beats a regression.

studies.title: Attribution surface for the threshold candidates
studies.question: What is the per-row attribution against the predictor value, for every variable a turning point is read off?
studies.attack: You cannot locate a threshold without showing the curve.

studies.title: Turning points, their intervals, and the gate swept
studies.question: Where does each curve cross zero, how wide is the interval, and does the stability verdict depend on where the gate was placed?
studies.attack: Your stability gate is a rule you invented, placed where it gives the answer you wanted.

studies.title: Whole-state holdout
studies.question: Can the model predict counties in states it has never seen?
studies.attack: County-grouped folds still let the model learn the state it is predicting.

studies.title: Residual spatial structure
studies.question: Is what the model fails to explain spatially random?
studies.attack: Your residuals are spatially autocorrelated, so your effective sample size is far smaller than three thousand counties.

studies.title: Collinearity and interaction among the leading variables
studies.question: How correlated are the leading variables, and how much of the attribution is interaction rather than main effect?
studies.attack: Eight of your fifteen leading variables have a variance inflation factor above ten.

studies.title: Mutual information census: the same question with no model
studies.question: Taken one column at a time against the outcome, with no model involved, which description carries more information?
studies.attack: Your central finding is a TreeSHAP artefact.
studies.note: This one answers the other way from the attribution census and is the reason the paper's claim is stated as conditional attribution rather than as informativeness.

studies.title: Rank stability and the learning curve
studies.question: How much does the attribution ranking move when the counties are resampled, and is the model still short of data?
studies.attack: Your ranking is one draw. Resample and the top ten will be a different top ten.

studies.title: Temporal validation: year holdout and forward chaining
studies.question: Can the model predict a year it has never seen, and can it predict forward in time rather than across counties?
studies.attack: Every fold of yours contains the year it predicts. This is interpolation in time dressed as prediction.

studies.title: Null calibration of the model's skill
studies.question: What score does this protocol return when the outcome is permuted and there is nothing to learn?
studies.attack: With 581 columns and repeated counties, 0.67 may be what your protocol returns on noise.
studies.note: Two permutations. Shuffling within county destroys the year signal and keeps the county mean; shuffling county labels destroys both. The gap between them is how much of the score is county identity.

studies.title: Does the crossing estimator find thresholds in noise?
studies.question: Run the whole crossing and gate procedure on permuted attribution. How often does it return a stable crossing?
studies.attack: A smoothing spline will cross zero somewhere in anything. Your eleven thresholds are an artefact of the estimator.
studies.note: The single most useful defence of the threshold half of the paper, and the one a methods referee will ask for first.

studies.title: Null for the census count
studies.question: If the central and non-central labels are shuffled within each field, how often does a count of 38 of 47 appear?
studies.attack: Thirty-eight of forty-seven sounds impressive until you know what the null is.

studies.title: The census under five attribution estimators
studies.question: Does the non-central lead survive changing the attribution method and the learner?
studies.attack: Interventional TreeSHAP with a 500-row background is one choice among several and the result is a property of that choice.
studies.note: Interventional SHAP, tree-path-dependent SHAP, split gain, permutation importance, and the same census on a second learner. If the count survives all five the artefact objection is closed.

studies.title: Satellite only, environment only, everything admitted
studies.question: How much of the skill is satellite-borne, and does the central finding hold inside the satellite-only panel?
studies.attack: This is a socioeconomic model with satellite decoration, and you have not separated the two.

studies.title: Leave-one-state-out jackknife of the census count
studies.question: Is the census count carried by one state?
studies.attack: Drop California and your 38 of 47 is 20 of 47.

studies.title: Influence: drop the counties the model relies on most
studies.question: Does the ranking hold when the most influential counties are removed?
studies.attack: A hundred unusual counties are driving this.

studies.title: Predictor perturbation and the located crossings
studies.question: If the predictors are perturbed at the magnitude of the reanalysis spread, how far do the turning points move?
studies.attack: These are reanalysis fields with their own error, and you report thresholds to three decimals.
studies.note: A sensitivity analysis on real values, reported as such. No perturbed column is written to any exported panel.

studies.title: What the admission gate is worth
studies.question: What does the score do if the gate is skipped, and what does it do if the protected columns are dropped?
studies.attack: Your gate is a filter you tuned until the score looked right.
studies.note: This is the arm that answers the question the whole package was rebuilt around: a run that skips the gate scores higher and the higher score means nothing.

studies.title: Formaldehyde pair: removal and inheritance
studies.question: When one of the pair is removed, does the other inherit its attribution, and what does the model lose?
studies.attack: Two columns correlated at 0.99 are one column. Drop either and nothing happens.

studies.title: The band test
studies.question: Can the difference between the two thresholds stand in for the pair?
studies.attack: If the pair is doing something a difference captures, say so and use the difference.

studies.title: Every other pair above the correlation cut
studies.question: Is the pair's behaviour particular to formaldehyde or general to protected pairs?
studies.attack: You have one anecdote and a mechanism invented to fit it.

studies.title: Matched refit of the summary-statistic arms
studies.question: With the column count held equal, does a panel of central summaries predict worse than a panel of non-central ones?
studies.attack: A ranking is not a prediction. Fit both and show me.

studies.title: Drop one night-cooling construction and refit
studies.question: What does the model lose when one of the two night-cooling variables is removed?
studies.attack: You kept both halves of a correlated pair. Show the cost of keeping only one.

studies.title: Reproducibility by rerunning
studies.question: Does a second run of the same script give the same numbers?
studies.attack: Gradient boosting is not deterministic and you have not shown this reproduces.
studies.note: Compares manifests rather than writing a result of its own, so the runner reports it as run only when its own manifest exists.

studies.title: Multiplicity over the declared family
studies.question: How many of the reported results survive control of the false discovery rate over every test this paper runs?
studies.attack: You ran a great many tests and reported the ones that worked.
studies.note: Cheap, but it has to run last: the family is assembled by reading the files the other studies write, and a correction over half of a family is not a correction.
